problems.title: Two branches of an absolute value
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of|2x−3|=9.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
steps: The roots are 6 and −3. Their sum is 3.

problems.title: Simplify before looking for a minimum
problems.question: For triangle angles a, b, c, minimise|3(a−2b)−5(a−3c)−4(c−b)−11c+4b|.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Collecting coefficients leaves$|-2a+2b|=2|b-a|$.
steps: An absolute value is at least0. Equality is possible with a=b, for example an equilateral triangle.

problems.title: Percentage growth versus percentage points
problems.question: Sports participation rises from 10% to 25% of an unchanged student population. Find the percentage increase in participants.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Increase/original=(25−10)/10.
steps: The ratio is 15/10=1.5, so the increase is 150%. The 15-percentage-point change is a different quantity.

problems.title: Angles between perpendicular bisectors
problems.question: Two triangle angles are 57°,67°. Which listed angle can occur between two side perpendicular bisectors?
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: The third angle is 180°−57°−67°=56°. Rotating both side directions90° preserves their line angle.
steps: The bisectors of the two sides meeting at that third vertex make56°, the listed possible value.

problems.title: Angles between two altitudes
problems.question: Altitudes from A and C make a 30° line angle. Which listed B angle is possible?
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Those altitudes are perpendicular to BC and AB. Their smaller line angle equals min(B,180°−B).
steps: Thus B can be30° or 150°. Of the listed options, only 30° appears.
problems.note: The geometry also permits150°; the question asks which listed value can occur.

problems.title: Inverse proportion
problems.question: Split470 into parts inversely proportional to 3,4,5. Find largest minus smallest.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
steps: The 47 ratio units total470, so one unit is 10. The parts are 200,150,120.
Their largest-minus-smallest difference is 80.

problems.title: Bound a largest member using distinct positive integers
problems.question: A has five distinct positive integers of mean10, B six distinct positive integers of mean10. Maximise|a−b| for a∈A, b∈B.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: The sums are 50 and 60. The other smallest distinct positive members give a≤50−(1+2+3+4)=40, b≤60−(1+2+3+4+5)=45.
steps: All members are at least1, so the absolute difference is at most45−1=44.
Choose A={1,2,3,4,40}, B={1,2,3,4,5,45}, and select a=1, b=45 to attain44.

problems.title: Evaluate absolute values with known signs
problems.question: Evaluate5|x−1.4|+3|x−7|−2(x−12) at x=1.99.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.

problems.title: The obtuse angle of an isosceles triangle is its apex
problems.question: An isosceles triangle ABC has C=100°. Find A.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Two angles of 100° cannot fit in a triangle, so C is the unique apex angle.
steps: The remaining equal angles sum to 80°, so each is 40°.

problems.title: Scale all three side lengths
problems.question: Triangle sides are proportional to 7,8,10; the smallest is 14. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: The scale factor is 14/7=2.
steps: The sides are 14,16,20. Their sum is 50 cm.

problems.title: Salt balance in a mixture
problems.question: Add50L of a salt solution to 30L of 10% solution to obtain5% solution. Find the added concentration.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Initial salt=3L-equivalent; final salt=(30+50)·0.05=4L-equivalent.
steps: The added50L contains1L-equivalent of salt. Its concentration is 1/50=0.02=2%.

problems.title: Guarantee colours remain after blind removal
problems.question: A box has 10 white,8 red,7 green pencils. What maximum percentage may be removed blindly while guaranteeing at least two of each colour remain?
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: The smallest colour group has 7 pencils. At most7−2=5 removals are safe in the worst case.
steps: Removing6 could remove six green pencils and leave only one. Removing5 cannot reduce any group below two.
There are 25 pencils, so the maximum percentage is 5/25=20%.

problems.title: Measure the second day against the remainder
problems.question: After20% of a job is done, what percentage of the remainder must be done to reach50% total?
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Remaining work=80%; extra work needed=30%.
steps: The requested proportion is 30/80=3/8=37.5%.

problems.title: Use both possible isosceles side patterns
problems.question: An integer-sided isosceles triangle has perimeter88, and unequal side lengths in ratio3:4. Find the shortest side.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: The two patterns are(3t,3t,4t) and(4t,4t,3t).
steps: The first gives t=8.8 and noninteger sides, so it is excluded. The second gives 11t=88, so t=8.
The sides are 32,32,24, and the shortest is 24.

problems.title: The smaller angle between two internal bisectors
problems.question: Triangle angles satisfy A+C=0.8B. Find the smaller angle between the A- and C-bisector lines.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: $1.8B=180^\circ$, so B=100°; the smaller bisector-line angle is 90°−B/2.
steps: Thus the required angle is 90°−50°=40°. The obtuse incenter angle is its supplement140°.

problems.title: Chain percentage changes
problems.question: a is 20% below b, c is 40% above a. By what percentage does the larger of b, c exceed the smaller?
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
steps: Thus c exceeds b by 0.12b, or 12%.

problems.title: Solve absolute values from the outside inward
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of|||3x−1|−1|+6|=7.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: The expression inside the outermost bars is at least6, so remove those bars.
steps: Then||3x−1|−1|=1, which gives|3x−1|=0 or 2.
The roots are 1/3,1,−1/3. Their sum is 1.

problems.title: Multiply successive retained fractions
problems.question: A merchant loses1/10 of goods at the first border,20% of the remainder at the second, and 1/3 of the remainder at the third. What percentage arrives?
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Retained fraction=$(9/10)(4/5)(2/3)$.
steps: Multiplication gives 72/150=12/25=0.48. Thus48% arrives.

problems.title: A circumcentre on a triangle side
problems.question: The perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC meet on AC. Find A+C.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Their intersection O satisfies OA=OB=OC and lies on AC, so O is the midpoint of AC.
steps: AC is a diameter of the circumcircle. The angle B subtending it is 90°.

problems.title: Use the small isosceles triangle in the angle chase
problems.question: AB=AC, E lies on AC, D on AE, ED=BE, and CBE=DBA. Find DBC.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Let base angle ABC=β and common angle CBE=DBA=t. Then DBE=β−2t.
steps: TriangleABD has angle A=180°−2β, so angle BDA=2β−t. Since DA and DE are opposite rays, BDE=180°−2β+t.
In triangle BDE, the equal sides BE=DE make the angles at D and B equal. Thus180°−2β+t=β−2t.
This givesβ−t=60°. But DBC=β−t, so the answer is 60°.

problems.title: Exactly seven positive divisors
problems.question: A counts two-digit numbers with 7 divisors, B three-digit numbers with 7 divisors. Find A·B.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Since7 is prime, a number with exactly 7 divisors must be p⁶ for a primep.
steps: 2⁶=64 is the only two-digit example;3⁶=729 is the only three-digit example;5⁶ already exceeds999.
Thus A=B=1 and A·B=1.

problems.title: An absolute-value equation equivalent to a single linear root
problems.question: The equations5x−2=2a+3b and|2x−1|=b are equivalent. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: The linear equation has exactly one root. The absolute-value equation has one root only when b=0.
steps: Then x=1/2. Substitute into5x−2=2a to get1/2=2a, so a=1/4.
Therefore a+b=1/4.

problems.title: Use the minimum extra books from five classes
problems.question: Thirty students from five represented classes bring40 books. Classmates bring equal positive counts, different classes different counts. How many bring one book?
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: One book each accounts for 30 books, leaving10 extras. Five different positive counts are at least1,2,3,4,5.
steps: At least one student from each of the four higher-count classes contributes at least1+2+3+4=10 extra books.
This uses every extra book, so those four classes contribute one student each, with counts2,3,4,5. The other 26 students bring one each.
problems.note: This uses the natural reading that each participating student brings at least one book.

problems.title: Equal distances in an equilateral configuration
problems.question: ABC is equilateral, M∈BC, N beyond C on AC, and AM=MN. What percentage of CN is BM?
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
steps: Squared distances give AM²=t²−t+1 and MN²=(1−t)²+(1−t)u+u².
Their equality simplifies to(u−t)(u+1)=0. Since u≥0, we getu=t.
Thus BM=CN and the requested percentage is 100%.

problems.title: Follow directions through two right angles
problems.question: In the shown diagram, KB∥FC, triangles KPL, FPN are right at L, N, BKL=47°, LPN=122°. Find NFC.
problems.idea: Convert the words into exact equations, and check which conditions the result needs.
formulas: Take the parallel lines horizontal. Since KL makes47° below horizontal, the perpendicular PL points 43° above horizontal.
steps: The ray PN then points 43°−122°=−79° relative to the horizontal.
FN is perpendicular to PN and points 11° above the rightward horizontal. Thus NFC=11°.
